ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: There are two spinners in the figure. The left one is Spinner A, divided into four regions labeled 1, 2, 3, 4; the right one is Spinner B, divided into three regions labeled 1, 2, 3. The problem states that the arrow on each spinner is equally likely to land on each number. Reasoning: It asks for the probability that the product of the numbers on the two spinners is even. Using the complement method, the opposite of the product being even is the product being odd, and the product is odd only when both numbers are odd. The odd numbers on Spinner A are 1 and 3, so P(A is odd)=2/4=1/2. The odd numbers on Spinner B are 1 and 3, so P(B is odd)=2/3. The two spins are independent, therefore P(the product is odd)=(1/2)(2/3)=1/3. So P(the product is even)=1-1/3=2/3.

raw_record.question_text:
Spinners A and B are spun. On each spinner, the arrow is equally likely to land on each number. What is the probability that the product of the two spinners' numbers is even?

<image1>

method.method_draft: First describe the image: Spinner A shows four labeled outcomes 1, 2, 3, and 4; Spinner B shows three labeled outcomes 1, 2, and 3. From the text, use that each listed number on a spinner is equally likely. Use the complement rule: the product is even unless both spinner results are odd. On A, the odd numbers are 1 and 3, so P(A odd)=2/4. On B, the odd numbers are 1 and 3, so P(B odd)=2/3. Because the spins are independent, P(product odd)=(2/4)(2/3)=1/3. Therefore P(product even)=1-1/3=2/3.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: Spinner A has possible results 1, 2, 3, 4, while Spinner B has possible results 1, 2, 3. From the text, treat all A-B result pairs as equally likely.
